Abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer treatment but commonly cause immune-related adverse events (irAEs), whether administered as monotherapy or in combina@on with other oncological agents. We present the ﬁrst reported case of ICI-induced granulomatous sialadeni@s in a male pa@ent in his mid-ﬁEies with BRAF-V600E-mutated papillary thyroid carcinoma who received sequen@al treatment with BRAF/MEK inhibitors followed by pembrolizumab. The pa@ent experienced acute-onset severe xerostomia and salivary hypofunc@on, promp@ng ICI cessa@on and salivary gland biopsy. Integra@ve analysis using histology, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spa@al transcriptomics revealed macrophage- and Tcell-mediated epithelial damage driven by epithelial senescence and Th1-polarized inﬂamma@on. Cor@costeroid therapy reduced granuloma burden and improved salivary ﬂow rates and @ssue architecture; however, extensive ﬁbrosis persisted despite treatment. These ﬁndings underscore the cri@cal importance of early irAE recogni@on and interven@on to preserve glandular func@on and enable con@nua@on of cancer therapy.

Introduc*on:

Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) restore an@tumor immunity by blocking inhibitory PD-1/PD-L1 interac@ons, enabling cytotoxic T cell-mediated tumor rejec@on (Postow et al., 2018). To enhance therapeu@c eﬃcacy, ICIs are frequently combined with CTLA-4 inhibitors, chemotherapies, or muta@on targeted small molecule inhibitors such as BRAF and MEK inhibitors (Hamidi et al., 2024). However, these therapies increase the risk of immune-related adverse events (irAEs) aﬀec@ng mul@ple organs, including the salivary glands, where clinical sialadeni@s occurs in 5-35% of pa@ents (Warner et al., 2019; Rosenberg et al., 2025). Due to limited epithelial regenera@ve capacity, ICI-induced inﬂammatory sialadeni@s can progress to chronic sicca syndrome (ICI-S) characterized by persistent salivary hypofunc@on and xerostomia (Warner & Baer, 2021). These complica@ons increase suscep@bility to oral infec@ons, impair quality of life, and may necessitate ICI discon@nua@on despite ongoing cancer treatment needs. While cor@costeroids provide temporary symptom relief, disease-modifying therapies remain elusive (Warner & Baer, 2021).

Here we report the ﬁrst case of ICI-associated granulomatous sialadeni@s (ICI-GS) in a pa@ent with BRAF-V600E-mutated papillary thyroid carcinoma treated sequen@ally with BRAF/MEK inhibitors followed by pembrolizumab. Granulomatous inﬂamma@on represents a

dis@nct immunological response involving organized epithelioid macrophage and T cell aggregates; this histological presenta@on has not been previously documented as an ICI complica@on in salivary @ssues, though it has been reported that BRAF/MEK inhibitors can induce sarcoid-like granulomas in skin and lung (Pham et al., 2022). We hypothesized that BRAF/MEK therapy established subclinical @ssue inﬂamma@on or altered immune regula@on, which was subsequently ampliﬁed by PD-1 blockade to trigger symptoma@c granulomatous sialadeni@s. To elucidate disease mechanisms and therapeu@c response, we analyzed minor salivary gland biopsies obtained at presenta@on and following a ﬁve-week cor@costeroid taper using integrated histological, single-cell RNA sequencing, and spa@al transcriptomic analyses.

Clinical Presenta.on and Sudden Onset of Severe Oral Dryness

A man in his mid-ﬁEies with metasta@c, poorly diﬀeren@ated papillary thyroid carcinoma (pT2N1bMx) underwent total thyroidectomy and radioac@ve iodine abla@on (Figure 1A, Supplemental Figure 1A). Six months postopera@vely, PET/CT imaging revealed lung and rib metastases, upstaging the disease to pT3b, pN1b, cM1. Molecular proﬁling iden@ﬁed BRAFV600E and TERT promoter muta@ons, promp@ng ini@a@on of combina@on BRAF/MEK inhibitor therapy with dabrafenib plus trame@nib. AEer nine months of stable disease with persistent residual metastases, pembrolizumab (200 mg intravenously every three weeks) was added to the regimen. Following three cycles of pembrolizumab, the pa@ent developed severe, acute-onset xerostomia that signiﬁcantly impaired ea@ng and sleep (Figure 1A, B). Pembrolizumab was discon@nued aEer the fourth infusion due to suspected immune-related salivary gland toxicity.

The pa@ent was subsequently referred to the NIDCR Sjögren's Disease Clinic for evalua@on, where examina@on revealed complete absence of s@mulated salivary ﬂow (CTCAE Grade 3 hypofunc@on) (Figure 1C). Minor salivary gland biopsies were obtained at this ini@al visit (designated ICI-GSpre).

Clinical Evalua.on and Histopathology

During BRAF/MEK inhibitor therapy, the pa@ent reported new-onset arthralgias aﬀec@ng the knees, feet, and ankles, but denied other systemic symptoms including cutaneous lesions, respiratory symptoms, or mucosal involvement. Laboratory evalua@on revealed no biochemical evidence of systemic granulomatous disease (Supplemental Table 1).

Salivary gland histopathology demonstrated marked sialadeni@s with immune-mediated epithelial injury and extensive, poorly organized non-necro@zing granulomas involving all of the submijed glands (Figure 1D). Notably, the granulomas lacked the characteris@c dense ﬁbrosis typical of sarcoidosis. Microbial stains (acid-fast bacilli, Grocoj methenamine silver, and periodic acid-Schiﬀ) were nega@ve; polarized light microscopy revealed no foreign material (Supplemental Figure 1B).

The inﬂammatory pajern and cellular composi@on were consistent with ICI-induced granulomatous inﬂamma@on (Figure 1D–E; Supplemental Figure 1B). Immunohistochemical analysis revealed granulomas composed of epithelioid macrophages (LCA⁺, CD68⁺) admixed with approximately equal numbers of CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells (CD3⁺). PD-1⁺ T cells were abundant within and surrounding granulomas, while PD-L1 expression was restricted to macrophages within granulomas and to ductal and acinar epithelium involved by granulomatous inﬂamma@on (Figure 1D–E). B cells (CD20⁺) and plasma cells (CD138⁺) were notably absent from the inﬂammatory inﬁltrate.

Clinical and Histological Response to Prednisone

The pa@ent was treated with oral prednisone ini@ated at 60 mg daily and tapered over ﬁve weeks. By day 36 of treatment, the pa@ent reported subjec@ve improvement in xerostomia with restora@on of the ability to eat solid foods without liquid assistance. Musculoskeletal pain also improved. Objec@ve salivary func@on tes@ng demonstrated marked improvement: uns@mulated whole saliva ﬂow increased from 0.0 to 3.6 mL/15 min (normal range: >1.5 mL/15 min), and s@mulated ﬂow increased from 1.2 to 3.3 mL/15 min (normal range: >7.5 mL/15 min) (Figure 1C).

Follow-up labial salivary gland biopsy obtained at day 36 (ICI-GS-post) demonstrated appreciable reduc@on in granuloma burden, with overall more organized granulomas with mean granuloma density decreasing from 2.2 to 0.7 per mm² and individual granuloma size reduced. The overall inﬂammatory inﬁltrate was markedly decreased with fewer epithelioid macrophages. T cells remained the predominant lymphocyte popula@on within residual granulomas, while CD20⁺ B cells remained sparse. Although both CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells persisted within granulomas,

Results: Immune-Engaged Epithelia and Inﬂamma.on Characterize ICI-GS and Resolve with Prednisone

Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of salivary gland @ssue obtained before and aEer prednisone treatment corroborated the histological ﬁndings and quan@ﬁed cellular changes induced by ICI therapy and subsequent cor@costeroid interven@on (Figure 2A). Following quality control, dimensionality reduc@on, unsupervised clustering, and cell type annota@on using established markers (Supplemental Figure 1C), cellular composi@on was compared across treatment condi@ons (Figure 2B).

The pre-treatment biopsy (ICI-GS-pre) demonstrated marked immune cell expansion compared to healthy control salivary glands. Total T cells increased from 4% to 34% of total cells (z-score = 10, p<0.001), CD8⁺ cytotoxic T cells from 3% to 10% (z = 3, p<0.01), and M1-polarized macrophages from 2% to 10% (z = 5, p<0.001). Conversely, acinar cells, which comprise the func@onal secretory parenchyma, were signiﬁcantly depleted from 58% in controls to 20% in ICIGS-pre (z = -2, p<0.05). Notably, a dis@nct popula@on of immune-engaged (IE) acinar cells emerged, represen@ng 15% of the total acinar compartment in ICI-GS-pre. These IE acinar cells exhibited gene expression signatures consistent with ac@ve T-cell-mediated targe@ng, including upregula@on of an@gen presenta@on machinery, interferon-s@mulated genes, and stress response pathways.

Following the ﬁve-week prednisone taper, the post-treatment biopsy (ICI-GS-post) revealed par@al normaliza@on of cellular composi@on, with immune popula@ons declining toward healthy propor@ons. Total T cells decreased from 34% to 18% (p<0.0001), CD8⁺ T cells from 10% to 9% (p=0.1), and M1-polarized macrophages from 10% to 5% (p<0.0001) (Figure 2B). The acinar compartment showed modest recovery, with non-IE acinar cells increasing from 20% to 24% of total cells (p<0.0001), while IE acinar cells declined from 15% to 12% of the acinar popula@on (p<0.0001), indica@ng par@al but incomplete resolu@on of epithelial immune engagement.

Epithelial Senescence and Immune Signaling Mark ICI-GS and Diminish with Cor.costeroid Therapy

To quan@fy epithelial senescence, we calculated a composite senescence index based on expression of established senescence-associated genes (Wang et al., 2025). The senescence index was signiﬁcantly elevated in ICI-GS-pre acinar cells compared to healthy controls (0.61 vs. 0.48, p<0.00001), driven by increased expression of canonical senescence markers including CDKN2A (p16INK4a), and senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP) components IFNG and IL1B (Figure 2D). Ligand-receptor interac@on analysis revealed extensive immune-epithelial crosstalk mediated by key inﬂammatory pathways including TNF, IFNG, and NOTCH signaling (Figure 2E). MHC class I-mediated interac@ons between epithelial cells and CD8⁺ T cells were markedly ampliﬁed in ICI-GS-pre and declined following cor@costeroid therapy, consistent with reduced CD8⁺ T cell inﬁltra@on. Collec@vely, these ﬁndings implicate epithelial senescence and sustained immune-epithelial interac@ons as central mechanisms driving granuloma forma@on and @ssue damage in ICI-GS. The novel granulomatous presenta@on and incomplete therapeu@c response prompted further inves@ga@on using spa@al transcriptomics to deﬁne @ssue architecture and cellular interac@ons in situ.

Spa.al Proﬁling Reveals Immune-Mediated Architectural Collapse and Recovery Following Prednisone Treatment

Spa@al transcriptomic analysis of ICI-GS @ssue revealed profound altera@ons in cellular composi@on and spa@al organiza@on compared with healthy salivary glands (Figures 2F, Supplemental Figure 1D,E). Pre-treatment ICI-GS specimens exhibited complete loss of normal glandular architecture, with granulomatous lesions dominated by M1-polarized macrophages and T cells. Following prednisone therapy, granulomas decreased markedly in both size and frequency (Figure 1D, Figures 2F–I).

Integra@on of spa@al transcriptomic data with matched histology revealed that granulomas showed polariza@on toward epithelial structures such as ducts and acini which showed histological and transcriptomic evidence of immune-mediated injury. M1-polarized macrophages within pre-treatment granulomas co-expressed epithelial markers, indica@ng ac@ve phagocytosis of dying glandular epithelium (Figures 2G–I). This ﬁnding provides direct molecular evidence for immune-mediated destruc@on of secretory @ssue in untreated ICI-GS.

Post-prednisone @ssue demonstrated substan@al reduc@on in overall immune inﬁltra@on, with decreased abundance of M1-polarized macrophages and T cells, accompanied by par@al restora@on of epithelial and stromal architecture (Figure 2B, Supplemental Figure 1D). However, immune cell popula@ons remained elevated rela@ve to healthy salivary gland controls, indica@ng incomplete immunological resolu@on. The post-treatment landscape was further characterized by increased ﬁbroblast accumula@on and expansion of B cell and plasma cell popula@ons following prednisone taper, consistent with ﬁbro@c remodeling and par@al normaliza@on of immune homeostasis (Figure 1D, Figures 2C,D).

Suppor@ng these results, spa@al neighborhood analysis of cellular interac@ons revealed re-establishment of physiological cell-cell associa@ons among ﬁbroblasts, acinar cells, ductal cells, and B-lymphocytes/plasma cells in post-treatment @ssue (Figures 2I,J; Supplemental Figures 1E,F). These interac@on pajerns demonstrate par@al restora@on of @ssue architecture and reduced immune-mediated injury. However, the combina@on of incomplete immunological resolu@on and sustained ﬁbro@c remodeling likely maintains residual epithelial cells in a senescent state, poten@ally limi@ng func@onal recovery despite this architectural reorganiza@on.

BRAF/MEK-Induced Senescence Primes Epithelium for T Cell Mediated Injury Following PD-1 Blockade

Integrated analysis of ICI-GS-pre salivary glands revealed Th1-polarized granulomatous inﬂamma@on (Figure 2C), suppor@ng a two-hit pathogenic model: BRAF/MEK inhibitors induced epithelial senescence during nine months of therapy (evidenced by elevated senescence index and SASP gene expression), establishing a pro-inﬂammatory microenvironment that was subsequently ampliﬁed by PD-1 blockade, unleashing T cell-mediated inﬂamma@on resul@ng in granulomas (Figure 2K). This hypothesis is consistent with the pa@ent's clinical course of subclinical systemic inﬂamma@on (arthralgias) during BRAF/MEK therapy followed by acute onset severe sialadeni@s within weeks of pembrolizumab ini@a@on.

The granulomatous inﬂamma@on exhibited a sarcoidosis-like molecular signature characterized by signiﬁcant upregula@on of NOD2 (nucleo@de-binding oligomeriza@on domain containing protein 2; p<0.001), a pajern recogni@on receptor that senses cellular stress and ac@vates granulomatous responses. Downstream NF-κB pathway components were coordinately upregulated, including NFKB1, NFKBIA, and RELA (all p<0.001), sugges@ng that senescenceassociated signals triggered NOD2-dependent granuloma forma@on (Murphy & Weaver, 2017).

Granuloma-associated macrophages demonstrated pronounced M1 polariza@on with elevated expression of pro-inﬂammatory markers: CD86, IL1B, TNF, and NOS2 (all p<0.001). Both CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells exhibited ac@vated cytotoxic eﬀector phenotypes with signiﬁcantly elevated cytotoxic molecules including PRF1 (perforin), GZMB (granzyme B), and IFNG (all p<0.001 vs. healthy controls).

Both T cell popula@ons demonstrated markedly elevated PDCD1 (in both CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cells; p<0.001), indica@ng sustained ac@va@on despite pembrolizumab blockade and sugges@ng chronic an@gen s@mula@on by senescent epithelial cells. Discussion: Epithelial Senescence and Immune Checkpoint Disrup.on Drive Granulomatous Inﬂamma.on

Our ﬁndings support a sequen@al two-hit model of pathogenesis. BRAF/MEK inhibitors induce cellular senescence and enhance an@gen presenta@on (Frederick et al., 2013), and our data suggest similar eﬀects in salivary epithelium. The elevated senescence index, upregula@on of SASP components, and loss of secretory genes indicate that nine months of BRAF/MEK therapy established widespread epithelial senescence. During this period, immune checkpoints likely restrained inﬂammatory responses, as evidenced by subclinical presenta@on with only arthralgias.

Pembrolizumab disrupted this balance, disinhibi@ng Tc/Th1 responses against senescent epithelium. The inﬂamma@on was characterized by NOD2-NF-κB pathway ac@va@on and a predominance of cytotoxic T cells including CD4⁺ T cells, rare outside chronic autoimmune condi@ons, alongside CD8⁺ T cells. Ligand-receptor analysis revealed extensive immune-epithelial crosstalk mediated by TNF, IFNG, and MHC class I interac@ons, driving granuloma forma@on (Figure 2K). Cri@cally, epithelial senescence persisted aEer cor@costeroid therapy, indica@ng that steroids suppress inﬂamma@on without reversing underlying epithelial pathology highligh@ng future therapeu@c direc@ons.

Prednisone treatment produced substan@al clinical improvements for the pa@ent including improvements in saliva@on and reduced feelings of a dry mouth, the ability to chew and swallow foods without the need to drink water between bites, reduced arthralgias. AEer prednisone, the glands demonstrated pathological improvement: granuloma burden decreased 68%, inﬂammatory inﬁltrates declined (T cells: 34%→18%; M1 macrophages: 10%→5%). However, post-treatment biopsies revealed extensive ﬁbrosis with acinar atrophy, and the acinar compartment remained severely depleted (24% vs. 58% in controls). This dissocia@on between inﬂammatory resolu@on and progressive ﬁbrosis likely reﬂects persistent senescent epithelium serving as a con@nuous source of pro-ﬁbro@c signals. Clinical Implica.ons

At 28-month follow-up, the pa@ent's disease had progressed, requiring alterna@ve therapies. Whether con@nued pembrolizumab would have provided durable disease control remains unknown. The irreversible glandular damage from delayed interven@on eliminated the possibility of ICI rechallenge, represen@ng a forced trade-oﬀ between quality of life and poten@ally life-prolonging therapy. This case emphasizes cri@cal medical needs including: (1) heightened surveillance for early salivary symptoms in ICI-treated pa@ents; (2) prompt cor@costeroid interven@on; (3) inves@ga@on of adjunc@ve senoly@cs/an@-ﬁbro@cs; and (4) biomarker development for risk stra@ﬁca@on to preserve both cancer therapy op@ons and quality of life.

## Conclusions:

We report the ﬁrst case of ICI-associated granulomatous sialadeni@s, a severe immunerelated toxicity arising from sequen@al BRAF/MEK inhibi@on and PD-1 blockade. Integrated singlecell, spa@al, and histologic analyses reveal that BRAF/MEK inhibitors induced epithelial senescence, which was subsequently ampliﬁed by pembrolizumab, unleashing cytotoxic T cells and M1 macrophages that drove granuloma forma@on and epithelial destruc@on.

While cor@costeroids reduced inﬂamma@on and par@ally restored salivary func@on, epithelial senescence persisted and ﬁbrosis developed, indica@ng incomplete recovery despite clinical improvement. These ﬁndings suggest that cor@costeroids alone are insuﬃcient and that early interven@on combining an@-inﬂammatory, senoly@c, and an@-ﬁbro@c strategies may be necessary to prevent irreversible glandular damage.

This case underscores a cri@cal clinical challenge: severe irAEs can necessitate discon@nua@on of poten@ally life-prolonging cancer therapies. The pa@ent's disease progression following pembrolizumab cessa@on highlights the importance of early recogni@on and aggressive management of salivary gland toxicity to preserve both quality of life and therapeu@c op@ons. Clinicians should maintain heightened surveillance for salivary and oral irAEs in pa@ents receiving ICIs, par@cularly following prior BRAF/MEK therapy.

Our experience demonstrates that integrated molecular approaches, combining single-cell transcriptomics, spa@al transcriptomic and proteomic proﬁling, and detailed histopathology, can elucidate irAE mechanisms and guide personalized management strategies for these increasingly common and complex immune toxici@es.
